- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly to capture mean reversion or rebound.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overcorrects downward; delay or reduce the magnitude of subsequent downward revisions.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility; smooth out forecast transitions if sentiment is neutral or weak.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period mean reversion; adjust downward in final 5–7 days if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with trend; align forecast with sentiment momentum rather than historical mean.
